The words

Peace! the welcome sound proclaim,
Dwell with rapture on the theme;
Loud, still louder, swell the strain:
Peace on earth, good will to men.

Breezes! whispering soft and low,
Gently murmur as ye blow,
Breathe the sweet celestial strain,
Peace on earth, good will to men.

Ocean's billows! far and wide
Rolling in majestic pride:
Loud still louder, swell the strain,
Peace on earth, good will to men.

Christians! who these blessings feel,
And in adoration kneel;
Loud, still louder, swell the strain,
Praise to God, good will to men.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum D and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on m (F♯), on the word “Peace”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 812 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Blessings of Peace”, where the book credits them to the Lewins Mead Collection.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to INNOCENTS; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.

  • Words: Anonymous
  • Melody: French Melody, 13th cent.
  • Music (1728): ascr., George Frederick Handel (died undefined)
  • Melody (1850): The Parish Choir, London

Tune INNOCENTS by ascr., George Frederick Handel (died undefined); words by Anonymous.

Sung to the same tune: Day by Day the Manna Fell, Forest Beasts, That Live by Prey, God of Mercy, Hear Our Prayer, Hail, All Hail the Joyful Morn, Hark, My Soul! It Is the Lord, In Thy Courts Let Peace Be Found, Lord, My Times Are in Thy Hand, Slowly, by God's Hand Unfurled, Softly Fades the Twilight Ray, Songs of Praise the Angels Sang, They, Who on the Lord Rely, When Before Thy Throne We Kneel, Winter Has a Joy for Me.

Questions about Peace! the Welcome Sound Proclaim

What is the doh of Peace! the Welcome Sound Proclaim?

In this version, in D major, doh is D. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Peace! the Welcome Sound Proclaim start on?

It starts on m (F♯ in D major), a pickup on the word “Peace” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to m.

Is Peace! the Welcome Sound Proclaim in the public domain?

Yes. ascr., George Frederick Handel died in undefined; the words were in print by 1853 and the music in 1728. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
